The fix is in `src/jinja2/idtracking.py`'s `Symbols.branch_update`. The old code tracked how many of an if/elif/else's branches stored each variable, and skipped re-resolving a variable's load if it was set in *every* branch â€” the optimization assumed "stored everywhere" meant "always safe as-is." That assumption broke for names that already had a load registered before the branch (e.g. a macro parameter, `VAR_LOAD_PARAMETER`): skipping the resolve step left the stale `param` load in place instead of re-deriving it, so the reference could evaluate to `undefined` at runtime.

The fix (matching the real upstream Jinja resolution) drops the per-branch counting/skip logic entirely: it just collects the union of names stored across branches, subtracts names already stored in the outer scope, and always resolves/aliases the rest â€” regardless of whether they were set in all, some, or one branch.

Verified: `tests/test_idtracking.py` (127 tests) and the full suite (782 tests, excluding two files that fail to collect due to an unrelated missing `attrs`/`trio` dependency in this environment) pass. Added a `CHANGES.rst` entry.
